hook.text: DNA origami survives only minutes in blood — nucleases chew it apart. Stability is the barrier to real-world use.

buildup.text: Magnesium ions stabilize origami in buffer — but physiological fluids have low magnesium, causing structures to unfold.

discovery.text: Chemical crosslinking locks the structure permanently — UV-activated psoralen stitches strands together covalently.

twist.text: Crosslinking sacrifices reconfigurability — a locked origami cannot open, switch, or respond to signals.

climax.text: Protein and lipid coatings shield origami from nucleases — bio-armor that preserves both structure and function.

punchline.text: DNA origami must survive the body to serve it — coatings are the key.

quiz.question: Why does unmodified DNA origami degrade quickly in blood?
options: Blood temperature is too high for DNA base pairing
Nuclease enzymes in blood digest the DNA strands, destroying the structure
Red blood cells physically crush the origami
